findings.problem: The plan deletes both the server-side reduction and names Bridge `_handle` as its duplicate, but never states where the surviving 'session-owned replay reducer at Bridge/RPC ingress' lives relative to the socket, nor how the other replay path keeps working. The two existing reducers serve different reconnect targets: server-side sess.extUIState replays widgets/statuses/dialogs to newly connected browser SSE clients, while the harness-side bridge uiState replays to a reconnecting pi-dish server socket. A single writer on one side cannot serve the other side's reconnect without an explicit cross-socket mechanism, and 'one replay-map writer' as the only proof could silently drop one replay path (e.g. SSE replay for a session whose bridge process is gone). Separately, no `_handle` symbol exists in the bridge; the reduction is inline in the RPC request handler, so the plan names a nonexistent seam.

report.summary: The plan is exceptionally well-grounded: the remaining inventory is complete and arithmetically exact (all 30 authored product JS files verified present and uniquely assigned across M1–M7; 42 core + 106 browser + 7 extension TS files confirmed; nine scripts confirmed), the three phases are distinct and finite with explicit deletion ledgers and a deliberate-exclusions list, and every refactor premise I spot-checked matches real code with exact line evidence. No contradictions found between phases, invariants, and dependency waves. One important gap at the M0 freeze gate — the Express/compression/ws declaration strategy is ambiguous in a way that could make M7's 'checked handlers' nominal — plus two minor decision-recording gaps; all three are textual fixes, not structural revisions.

findings.section: M0 — Freeze delivery, contracts and coverage inventory
findings.problem: The typing mechanism for the entire HTTP surface is left ambiguous at the contract-freeze gate everything else inherits. 'Add compatible Express 4, compression and ws declarations for their actual implementations; use the real node-pty/Electron/package declarations' contrasts hand-maintained declarations for express/compression/ws against 'real' declarations for node-pty/Electron, implying a hand-authored Express facade. M7 moves all ~5,400 lines of routes into checked code against this facade; a hand-rolled Express 4 surface (middleware augmentation, req/res extensions, express.json limits) is a large, drift-prone replacement for the battle-tested pinned @types/express@4, and any gap in it pressures exactly the 'no any' workaround the plan bans. The risk that a hand-written facade is vacuous or ballooning is unproven, but the ambiguity itself is proven and M0 exists to freeze exactly this decision.

M7 acceptance: 'every baseline server handler has a checked implementation' — meaningfulness depends on this facade

report.summary: The plan is unusually well-grounded: I independently reproduced its headline measurements from the working tree (42 src/core TS files ≈ 447 KB; authored lib 217.9 KB + server.js 238.6 KB → 49.49% backend TS, matching the stated 49.5%; 23 authored lib JS + server.js + 6 edge implementations = 30 files ≈ 536.8 KB ≈ the stated 549,637 bytes; 106 browser + 42 core + 7 extension TS = 155), and every one of the twelve refactors I spot-checked maps to the exact duplicated responsibility it claims to delete (routines rereads, per-section coveredLines, checked* projection wrappers, tolerant mining loop, duplicate omp-export decoder, seven closeOtherViews peer lists, per-mutation createSessionApi, vendor __mods/__cache/__req loader, serverCloseHooks + Electron 300 ms, four relay timer/settle sites, file-page escapeHtml, skill-client ref copies). Migration, simplification and repository closure are genuinely separate, finite and gated, and the invariants preserve authority/framing/wire boundaries rather than relaxing them. It is not yet ready to start M6/integration work: three gates assert outcomes the repository cannot currently evaluate (no `any` enforcement path, no typed source for OMP/Prime host-only surfaces, no stated rule for where edge TS sits relative to packaged/installed trees), plus four smaller specification gaps. All are clarifications that can be resolved inside M0; none invalidate the plan's structure.

findings.section: Invariants and scope limits / M6a acceptance
findings.problem: The plan bans `any`/`@ts-nocheck`/unchecked declaration workarounds and requires M6a files to be 'checked by CI, not just transpiled', but nothing in the repository can reject explicit `any`. Strict `tsc` accepts it, and the lint config only loads JS: eslint.config.js:26 lints `files: ['**/*.js','**/*.cjs','**/*.mjs']` with espree (no TS parser), and package.json devDependencies contains no typescript-eslint. Extension sources that M6a must check already carry broad `any` over host objects (extensions/pi-dish-bridge/core.ts:663 `handler: async (_args: string, ctx: any)`, core.ts:872-877 `new Map<string, any>()` for uiState widgets/statuses/title/editorText), so the gate is unobservable today.
